note: Re-judged 2026-10-30 by an independent auditor after the userns conversion. The unit's only change since the last verdict is userns.Enter(t) as its first statement (the child re-runs the whole body in its own user, network and mount namespace; a child failure or skip propagates to the parent, and a child that ran nothing fails it) plus removal of EPERM/EACCES skips, so a refused privilege now fails instead of skipping. Assertions are byte-identical. Section 2.0: 'More importantly, the sending of signatures must be under the complete control of the application, not at the mercy of the remote host not understanding the option.' Positive TestRFC2385UnsignedSYNACKDoesNotDisableSignatures: the key the application installed survives an unsigned SYNACK (signed retransmission, dial timeout). Negative TestRFC2385UnconfiguredSocketSendsNoSignature: with no key, RealDialer and the listener complete an ordinary handshake, any Kind 19 on a captured segment fails it, and two SYN-bearing packets are required. Config units TestRFC2385ConfiguredKeyReachesBothSockets and TestRFC2385NoKeyWithoutConfiguration (unchanged) bind the key to configuration.
